holdout.rule: No holdout is withheld: every rule is fixed from the literature and no parameter is fitted. Out-of-sample is defined by publication date. pre_1999 (through 1998-12-31) is the pre-publication sample of Moskowitz-Grinblatt (JF 1999); 1999_2011 and 2012_latest are post-publication windows; post_1999 is their union. The holdout block records the post-publication window start and the prereg date as the end bound. The run is executed once per data vintage; a re-run on the same vintage must reproduce the report, and any rule, period or cost change is a new prereg.

hypothesis: The canonical trend rules (12-month excess-return sign; price above the 10-month average) and 12-1 month industry momentum (top 3, long-only, cash filter) earned a positive excess Sharpe on 1926+ US industry portfolios before publication, and the post-publication Sharpe is lower by a McLean-Pontiff style decay that is measured, not assumed. Reported alongside: equal-weight industries rebalanced monthly (primary comparator) and buy-and-hold equal weight. This is replication evidence for the sleeve priors in plan/appendix/11; it gates no sleeve.
limits: The prereg_v1 validator cannot express this design: (1) cost_model_version accepts only cost_v2, which prices US ETF fills off NBBO quotes; this study charges a proportional 10 bp per side on industry legs (2x stress: 20 bp) because French data has no spreads, so the field carries cost_v2 only to pass validation and the real model is in the signal text and cost_bp_per_side; (2) split/holdout describe a publication-date split, not a walk-forward or a withheld tail; (3) min_net_sharpe, max_drawdown_pct, min_cost_multiple, min_days and new_signal_tstat_min are reused for descriptive pass flags (evaluate_criteria), not for a gate; post_publication_tstat_min is an extra key the validator ignores. research/strategy/prereg.py is frozen and was not changed. The trial ledger is not written: these are replication runs on published rules, not A-gate trials, and are counted here as N=3 rules; whether they enter the global N is an open decision.
signal: research/strategy/long_history.py, target functions reused unchanged from research.strategy.sleeves. ts_ma10: trend.ma10, hold an industry (1/N slot) iff its month-end total-return index exceeds its 10-month average, else the slot earns the risk-free rate. ts_mom12: trend.mom12_vs_tbill, hold iff the 12-month return beats the 12-month risk-free return. xs_mom12_1: sector_mom.mom12_1, top 3 industries by 12-1 month return at 1/3 each, a slot is cash when that return does not beat cash; long-only, no leverage. Decided from data through the month-end close t; earns returns from session t+1 (entry at the close of t). Cost 10 bp of traded notional per side on industry legs, cash legs free; 2x stress at 20 bp; one extra session of delay reported as a disclosed robustness block. Evaluation starts after the 14th month-end; a final month with fewer than 15 sessions is dropped. Excess return is monthly (compounded daily rule return minus compounded RF). Statistics: annualised excess return, vol, Sharpe (sqrt 12), max drawdown on the daily total-return curve, Newey-West t, stationary-bootstrap 95% CIs (B=2000, seed 20260930), active return versus ew_monthly, decay ratio Sharpe(post)/Sharpe(pre) with independent-bootstrap CI and the Sharpe difference; windows post_1999, 1999_2011, 2012_latest and rule_pub (ts_ma10 2007, ts_mom12 2012, xs_mom12_1 1999). Descriptive flags at decision thresholds: replicates_pre_1999 (Sharpe >= 0.3 and HAC t >= 3.0), survives_post_1999 (Sharpe >= 0.3 and HAC t >= 2.0), positive_at_2x_cost_post_1999, max_dd_within_limit_post_1999 (<= 50%), active_ci_lower_gt_0_post_1999. Universe: industries with no missing (-99.99) daily return in the file, at least 12. Data: Kenneth French Data Library 49_Industry_Portfolios_daily (value-weighted block) and F-F_Research_Data_Factors_daily (RF), sha256 in the fetch manifest. No parameter may change after the first real-data run.
universe: French 49_Industry_Portfolios_daily value-weighted, industries with complete history
